name: Alcohol cutting (quit drinking)
lead: Alcohol cutting means reducing or stopping alcohol, a change looksmaxxing communities discuss as a way to look less puffy and to improve skin. The idea is a short chain: less alcohol leads to better hydration and sleep, which leads to a fresher, less swollen face, and removing the calories in drinks also supports leaner body composition.

Reference sources describe alcohol as suppressing vasopressin, the antidiuretic hormone, so the body loses more water in urine; the same sources say stopping drinking restores hydration and may benefit skin appearance [1]. Alcohol also disrupts sleep patterns, including later REM sleep, and sleep quality often improves after people stop [1].

Alcohol is also a recognised trigger of facial flushing. Acetaldehyde, a breakdown product of alcohol, causes the flush reaction that is common in people carrying an ALDH2 gene variant [1], and alcohol is listed among the triggers of flushing episodes in rosacea [2]. People who see redness after drinking sometimes cut alcohol for that reason.
No published trial has measured facial appearance before and after quitting alcohol; the evidence is made up of general physiology and health-outcome research.

sections.h: How it is used for appearance
paras: Practitioners range from giving up alcohol entirely to dropping it during a cut or in the weeks before photos or events. Communities describe the target effects as a leaner, less swollen face on waking, calmer skin tone, and better recovery from training.
Because alcoholic drinks supply calories with little fullness per calorie, removing them lowers total energy intake, which is the route to a leaner look [1].
Alcohol reduces the release of vasopressin, increasing water loss and contributing to dehydration and hangover thirst; stopping drinking restores hydration [1].

Alcohol disrupts normal sleep patterns, and sleep quality, including later REM stages, often improves after stopping [1]. Fatigue is among the factors dermatology references list as making skin look paler and under-eye circles more visible [4].

The alcohol flush reaction is driven by acetaldehyde and is most associated with an ALDH2 variant carried by an estimated 30 to 50 percent of people of Chinese and Japanese ancestry [1]. In rosacea, alcohol is one of several listed triggers of flushing that can last more than ten minutes [2].

Reference sources describe liver repair, lower blood pressure and lower risk of several cancers after stopping, with changes beginning within weeks and continuing over months and years [1]. The International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies alcoholic beverages as a Group 1 carcinogen [3].

No studies found directly measuring facial appearance after quitting alcohol. Related clinical research covers alcohol cessation and outcomes in other settings: a Cochrane review examined alcohol-cessation interventions before surgery and postoperative complications [5], and a clinical review covers management of alcohol misuse in people with liver disease [6].

People with heavy or long-term alcohol dependence can experience serious withdrawal, and clinicians generally advise medical supervision in that situation. Case reports describe withdrawal-related neurological complications [7].

card.summary: Quitting or cutting alcohol for less puff and better skin; the face effect itself is little studied.
card.note: Heavy drinkers should not stop abruptly without medical advice.

quick.overview:
Cutting alcohol is a common recommendation in appearance communities for reducing puffiness.

Sources describe benefits for hydration, sleep and weight, but direct facial studies are lacking.
quick.mechanism: Alcohol suppresses vasopressin, promotes fluid loss, disrupts sleep and adds calories [1].
quick.risks: Withdrawal can be dangerous in dependent drinkers.
